_any.shape: Answer or decision in the first 3 lines; the piece the reader will use next; then at most 3 supporting parts; any assumption that changes what to do in one line next to the part it affects.
_any.notes: Use only when no family fits; a shorter answer that is dense still loses, so cut codes and repeated rationale before cutting usable parts.

paid-social-ads.shape: The asked number of concepts, each: primary text 40-90 words with the hook in the first 125 characters, headline within the platform limit (about 40 characters), image brief 2-4 lines; any required disclosure short and fitted inside each ad; shared offer details and build specs said once; a test plan only if the brief asks for one.
paid-social-ads.notes: Dev: 1.29x won only 5 of 8 because every ad repeated the same definition and disclaimer block; say shared lines once, keep each required disclosure short, keep each ad as short as a feed scroll allows.

landing-page.shape: Hero (headline, subhead, one CTA) above the fold; 4-6 sections in order problem, how it works, proof, offer, FAQ (4-6 questions), final CTA; legal lines small in the footer.
landing-page.notes: Dev: 0.93x won 8 of 8; judges still flagged the legal text as heavy, so keep required disclosures but put them in the footer, not the selling sections.

lifecycle-email.shape: Each email: subject, preview text, body 120-200 words with one job and one CTA; then a build table of at most 10 rows and one line on what to watch, unless the brief asks for a measurement plan.
lifecycle-email.notes: Dev: 0.70x still lost 3 of 8 because the emails read like dense notices; warm customer-voice copy first, operational detail only in the build table.

competitor-analysis.shape: Verdict and the single biggest weakness first; one comparison table (rows = competitors, columns = the asked dimensions); 3-5 actions ranked by money per unit of effort, each with an owner and a day relative to the start; compact source list.
competitor-analysis.notes: Dev: 1.02x won 8 of 8 but was called very dense; the table and the actions earn the words, not more prose per row.

support-macros.shape: One macro per asked ticket type, each: when to use (1 line), customer reply 50-150 words for email or 1-3 lines for chat, agent steps 2-4 lines; then one escalation table.
support-macros.notes: Dev: 1.27x won 8 of 8 but clarity fell about 2 points from codes and abbreviations; agents must load a macro in seconds, so spell everything out and keep each macro short.

creative-brief.shape: One page: objective, audience and tension, single-minded message, reasons to believe with sources, tone with one example line, mandatories, deliverables table with specs, timeline table with owners.
creative-brief.notes: New in v3.3 after the 12 Nov fresh set routed an agency brief to the lifecycle-email card. One page means one page; strategy belongs in a separate note only if asked.

analysis-memo.shape: Recommendation box first; the numbers with inputs and one worked example; what the data does and does not show; ranked options or hypotheses; risks with mitigations; decision rule, owners and days relative to the start (calendar dates only when the brief gives them).
analysis-memo.notes: New in v3.3 after the 12 Nov fresh set routed an analysis memo to experiment design and a finance memo to the generic card. Show every calculation step; keep to the asked length.

notification-copy.shape: One row per asked message: moment or trigger, title and body (or the exact string), character counts, action or deep link; then one line on which to send first and one short cadence and stop note.
notification-copy.notes: New in v3.3 for push, SMS, in-app and UI copy. The v3 dev push task lost 0 of 4 and the fresh microcopy task 1 of 4 on the generic card; length must stay at or under plain.

sales-pitch.shape: Buyer page no longer than the plain answer's pitch (one page means about 450 words): headline ask, why now, proof (3 points), the specific ask, what we commit, next step; a separate labeled rep kit after it.
sales-pitch.notes: Dev: the buyer-facing page won when it stayed short; the seller's kit sits in a clearly separate section and shares the same overall budget.

claims-review.shape: Summary table first (claim, risk level, verdict); then per claim: risk, reason with the rule in 1-2 lines, and a paste-ready rewrite; one short what-evidence-would-clear-it box.
claims-review.notes: Dev: 0.90x won 8 of 8; the rewrites and the rule citations are what the reader uses, so cut background on the law, not the rewrites.

experiment-design.shape: Short version first (arms, primary metric, sample size, duration, decision rule in at most 150 words); then sections in the asked order with one worked sample-size calculation and one decision table.
experiment-design.notes: Dev: 0.84x won only 4 of 8 because jargon and density hid the plan; define each metric once in plain words and make the primary metric match the decision.

creator-brief.shape: Creator-facing part at most 700 words: the product in one line, do and don't card, 3-5 video formats, disclosure rules, deliverables and due days; deal terms and review checklist as a separate short section.
creator-brief.notes: Dev: 1.22x won 8 of 8 but every judge called it long for creators; keep the required compliance rules, trim everything else the creator does not act on.

crisis-response.shape: The decision in 2 lines, then the reply to post (within the platform limit, at most 120 words) that answers the charge head-on, then a 72-hour plan table (time, action, owner, trigger); at most 2 reply variants.
crisis-response.notes: Dev: 1.04x won only 4 of 8; judges wanted less density and a direct answer to the accusation, since the reader acts within hours.

outbound-sales.shape: Each email 50-120 words with one ask and its send day; one compliant footer stated once; then optional usable kit (personalization guide, reply scripts, short pilot plan).
outbound-sales.notes: Dev: the emails won because each was shorter than the plain answer's; a seller's kit earns space only inside the owner's limit, after the emails.

help-docs.shape: Short answer up top; who does what and when (table); numbered steps by method; what does not carry over; FAQ of 5-8 questions; no internal notes in the published text.
help-docs.notes: Dev: extra steps and limits paid off where readers would otherwise file tickets, but clarity fell 1 point; spend words on steps, not background.

pricing.shape: Recommendation and price first; one comparison table; 2-3 revenue scenarios; the gates and test before any change; customer-facing wording in at most 5 lines.
pricing.notes: Dev: 0.91x won 8 of 8 but clarity fell 1.6 points from a wall of figures; show the few numbers the decision turns on and move the rest to the table.

job-description.shape: 400-700 words: role in 2-3 sentences, what you will do (5-7 bullets), what you bring (5-7), nice to have (2-3), pay and benefits, hiring process steps.
job-description.notes: Dev: 1.07x won 8 of 8; candidates skim on a phone, so specific bullets beat a longer story about the team.

webinar-script.shape: Timed outline table first (segment, minutes, speaker, goal); talk track at about 130-150 spoken words per minute of the asked length; cues in brackets; follow-up email last.
webinar-script.notes: Dev: 0.92x won 7 of 8 plus 1 tie; judges called it heavy to run, so cues stay short and the script never exceeds the spoken time.

review-replies.shape: Public reply (praise 20-50 words, complaints 40-90) that thanks, answers one point with one fact, and invites contact; then the internal plan (owner, action, day) and platform rules on contacting reviewers.
review-replies.notes: Dev: 0.93x won 8 of 8; the short public reply won and the plain answer's long feature list in the reply was marked down.

seo-article.shape: Answer the search question in the first 100 words; H2s that match real sub-questions; one table or list where readers compare; FAQ of 3-5; title and meta description within search limits.
seo-article.notes: No dev data; length follows search intent and the pages that already rank, never padding to hit a word count.

social-calendar.shape: One table: day (the brief's dates when it gives them), channel, format, hook, caption, asset, CTA; captions at native length for each channel; a 3-5 line note on themes and cadence.
social-calendar.notes: No dev data; the calendar is scanned row by row, so every post fits one row and strategy prose stays short.

launch-plan.shape: Goal and launch day first (the brief's date when it gives one); phases (before, launch day, after) as a table with owner, day relative to launch and done-when; standard safety gates (staged rollout, undo) inside the plan; risks with triggers; success measures (3-5).
launch-plan.notes: No dev data; each row must be a task someone owns, and the plan stays within the owner's limit.

investor-update.shape: Monthly 300-600 words, quarterly up to about 900: one-line summary, key metrics table, wins (3), problems (2-3) told straight, cash and runway, specific asks (1-3).
investor-update.notes: No dev data; investors read many updates, so numbers and asks up front and no narrative padding.

research-design.shape: Decision the research informs first; 3-5 questions; method and sample with reasons; recruiting criteria; discussion guide or instrument; analysis plan and timeline.
research-design.notes: No dev data; the guide and screener are usable parts that earn space, background theory does not.

product-announcement.shape: Press release 300-500 words, customer email 100-200: headline, what it is in one line, 3 benefits with a concrete example each, who gets it and when, how to start, one CTA.
product-announcement.notes: No dev data; readers decide in seconds whether it matters to them, so lead with the change and cut company backstory.

partnership-pitch.shape: Outreach note at most 150 words with one ask; then a one-page proposal (about 450 words): fit, what each side gets, first small test, next step.
partnership-pitch.notes: No dev data; follows the sales-pitch evidence that a short partner-facing page wins and extras belong in a separate section.

onboarding-flow.shape: Activation goal first; one table of steps (day or trigger, channel, message, goal); in-product messages at most 40 words, emails 100-150 words; metrics per step.
onboarding-flow.notes: No dev data; follows the lifecycle-email evidence that each message has one job and operational detail lives in the table.

press-pitch.shape: Subject line of about 10 words or fewer that states the story; body 100-200 words: news hook and angle in 2 sentences, why this reporter in 1 line, what is offered, embargo terms if any, one ask, contact; an optional 2-3 sentence follow-up.
press-pitch.notes: New in v3.4 after the 13 Nov fresh set found no fitting card. A reporter judges it in seconds, so the story leads and company backstory is cut.

rfp-response.shape: One row per question in the buyer's order: number, answer (Yes, No, Partly, Planned), how it works in 1-3 sentences, evidence with date, scope or limits, owner; any answer that rests on an assumption says so in one line; within any word limit the buyer sets.
rfp-response.notes: New in v3.4 after the 13 Nov fresh set found no fitting card. Answer first and evidence per line earn length; marketing prose does not.

sop.shape: Header (number, version, owner, effective and review dates); purpose and scope in 2 lines; roles table; before you start; numbered one-action steps with checks inline; exceptions table; records table.
sop.notes: New in v3.4 after the 13 Nov fresh set found no fitting card. Staff follow it on shift, so one action per step and no background prose.

product-description.shape: Title; 1-2 sentence benefit lead; 3-6 benefit bullets; specs table from the source; fit or size and care; what is in the box; shipping and returns line; 120-300 words of copy plus the table.
product-description.notes: New in v3.4 after the 13 Nov fresh set found no fitting card. Shoppers scan, so specs live in the table and no claim goes past the source.

audio-ad-script.shape: Header with slot length, word count at about 150 words a minute (about 75 words for 30 seconds), format, offer, code and URL; the script or talking points with the code and URL said twice; must-say and must-not-say lines; read notes.
audio-ad-script.notes: New in v3.4 after the 13 Nov fresh set found no fitting card. The slot length is a hard limit; the word count must fit it.

internal-announcement.shape: Subject that names the change; what changes in the first 2 sentences, when, who it affects, why, numbered actions with due days, where to ask; 150-400 words; manager notes or FAQ only if asked, labeled and separate.
internal-announcement.notes: New in v3.4 after the 13 Nov fresh set found no fitting card. Every employee reads it once, so the change and the action lead and context stays short.

vendor-scorecard.shape: Recommendation box first (choice, why, top risk); the need in 2-3 lines; deal-breakers pass or fail table; criteria and weights table fixed before scoring; scoring table with evidence per score; totals and sensitivity; risks and next steps with owners.
vendor-scorecard.notes: New in v3.4 after the 13 Nov fresh set found no fitting card. The tables carry the work; extra length is earned only by evidence per score.

policy-doc.shape: Header (owner, version, effective and review dates); purpose and scope; key terms; numbered rules written as condition then action; limits and approvals table; examples table with edge cases; escalation table.
policy-doc.notes: New in v3.4 after the 13 Nov fresh set found no fitting card. Rules must be testable; values statements with no rule do not earn length.

localisation-brief.shape: One to two pages: project summary; audience and use per locale; tone with one example line; terms to keep and never translate; glossary table; length and format rules table; legal and cultural flags; review steps and timeline.
localisation-brief.notes: New in v3.4 after the 13 Nov fresh set found no fitting card. The glossary and length rules are the usable parts; background on the brand stays short.
